# Best 65W GaN chargers for a laptop and phone

**My pick: Anker 735 Charger (Nano II 65W)**, $29.99 at Newegg: https://www.newegg.com/p/359-00D8-002C3

- It has 2 USB-C ports and 1 USB-A, and delivers a full 65W to one device.
- Anker's spec sheet says laptop plus phone on the two USB-C ports splits 45W + 20W. That's fine for a MacBook Air or Dell XPS 13-class laptop while the phone charges.
- It has foldable prongs and is about the size of an AirPods Pro case. The two reviews I found from laptopbee.com rank the Anker 65W 3-port (GaN II) as their top pick, though their quoted port splits conflict with Anker's own specs, so I used Anker's.
- Sources: [Anker spec page](https://service.anker.com/product-description/a085g000004x2BVAAY), [Newegg listing](https://www.newegg.com/p/359-00D8-002C3), [Laptopbee](https://www.laptopbee.com/best-65w-usb-c-chargers/)

## Alternatives

- **Baseus Enercore 67W (CJ11), about $29.99.** Tom's Hardware named it the best 65W-range charger after testing. It held full wattage throughout testing and ran the coolest of the group. It also has a built-in retractable USB-C cable plus two more USB-C ports, which is handy for travel. Pricing and purchase links: https://www.tomshardware.com/peripherals/usb/best-usb-chargers
- **UGREEN Nexode Pro 65W.** One review site's top pick for travel: 113g, three ports, with US/UK/EU plug heads in the box. With two devices connected, independent testing shows a 45W + 20W split. See the pick and price links here: https://smartgadgetkit.com/best-gan-charger/
- **Baseus GaN5 Pro 65W, $49.99 for a 2-pack.** It's a good choice if you want one charger for home and one for your bag, or if you own a Samsung Galaxy, because it supports PPS. The catch is that with multiple devices connected, the laptop port drops to 45W. Details: https://dealectric.com/baseus-gan5-pro-65w-2c-u (that page uses affiliate links).

## Things to know

- A "65W" charger only gives the full 65W to one device. Once the phone is also plugged in, the laptop port drops to about 45W. That's fine for most thin-and-light laptops, but a laptop that needs a full 65W will charge more slowly while you also charge your phone.
- If you use a Samsung phone and want its fastest charging, pick a model with PPS. The Anker 735 lists PPS support, and so does the Baseus GaN5 Pro.
- Chargers rarely include cables, so you may need a USB-C cable rated for 60W or more.

If you tell me which laptop and phone you have, I can say whether 65W is enough or whether a 100W model would be better.
